**Creating an egg and tomato recipe**

The user wants to know how to cook eggs and tomatoes together. I’ll provide a recipe for classic Chinese-style scrambled eggs with tomatoes and consider variations like Western-style scrambled eggs, baked eggs in tomato sauce (shakshuka), and an omelette with tomatoes. I aim to keep it concise, including essential ingredients, steps, tips, timing, seasonings, and optional additions, while being sure to give the right proportions and cooking times. Here are three simple, tasty ways to cook eggs and tomatoes together — choose one by style and time.

1) Chinese-style Tomato and Egg Stir-Fry (quick, common)
Ingredients (serves 2)
- 3–4 eggs
- 2 medium tomatoes (or 3 small), roughly chopped or cut into wedges
- 1–2 scallions (optional), sliced
- 1–2 cloves garlic (optional), minced
- 1–2 tsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp salt (adjust)
- 1–2 tbsp oil
- A splash of soy sauce or fish sauce (optional)
- 1 tbsp water (optional) to make a light sauce

Method
1. Beat eggs with a pinch of salt.
2. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or skillet over medium-high. Pour in eggs, scramble quickly until just set but still soft, then transfer to a plate.
3. Add another tbsp oil. Sauté garlic briefly, add tomatoes, and cook 2–4 minutes until softened and juicy. Sprinkle sugar and a little salt to balance acidity.
4. Return eggs to the pan, toss gently with tomatoes. Add a splash of water if you want a bit of sauce. Cook 30–60 seconds to combine.
5. Stir in scallions and a dash of soy/fish sauce if using. Serve hot with rice or toast.

Tips: Use ripe tomatoes for sweetness. Keep eggs slightly underdone in the first step so they stay tender.

2) Western-style Tomato Scramble (fast breakfast)
Ingredients (serves 1–2)
- 4 eggs
- 1 medium tomato, diced
- 2 tbsp milk or cream (optional)
- Salt & pepper
- 1 tbsp butter or oil
- Fresh herbs (basil/parsley), grated cheese optional

Method
1. Whisk eggs with milk, salt, pepper.
2. Melt butter in a nonstick pan over medium. Add diced tomato, cook 1–2 minutes.
3. Pour eggs in, let set slightly, then gently fold until creamy and cooked to preference.
4. Finish with herbs or cheese.

3) Baked Eggs in Tomato Sauce (Shakshuka-inspired, great for sharing)
Ingredients (serves 2–3)
- 1 tbsp oil
- 1 onion (optional), sliced
- 1 bell pepper (optional), diced
- 2–3 garlic cloves, minced
- 400 g (1 can) crushed tomatoes or 4 fresh tomatoes, chopped
- 4 eggs
- Paprika, cumin, salt, pepper, chili flakes to taste
- Fresh herbs, feta (optional)

Method
1. Sauté onion and pepper until soft. Add garlic and spices, cook 30 sec.
2. Add tomatoes, simmer 8–10 minutes until slightly reduced. Taste and adjust seasoning.
3. Make wells in the sauce, crack eggs into wells. Cover and simmer on low 6–10 minutes until whites set and yolks to your liking (or bake at 180°C/350°F covered until done).
4. Top with herbs and cheese, serve with bread.

General tips
- Balance tomato acidity with a bit of sugar or salt.
- Cook eggs gently for tender texture.
- Add protein (ham, tofu) or greens (spinach) for variety.
- Use ripe tomatoes for best flavor; canned tomatoes work well in shakshuka.

Tell me which style you prefer (quick stir-fry, breakfast scramble, or baked) and I can give a scaled recipe or timing for a specific serving size.
